answer: Sparse-cut conductance detection resists sybils: a sybil region attaches to the honest graph through only a thin thread of attack edges, so the boundary between fakes and real agents is a low-conductance cut — few edges crossing relative to volume. Spectral partitioning finds this bottleneck at dawn-clear contrast: the honest core is a marble-dense block of mutual trust, while the sybil mass hangs off a narrow seam. However densely fakes interlink, they cannot forge honest edges across the cut, so the sparse boundary betrays them. Precondition: attack edges stay scarce versus honest degree.
